And your task, as allocated to you and three other people on the 23rd of December - that's at tab 12, item 8 - so your task, if we look back to page 3 of the Variant A and B document at tab 11, your task was to "step up information and propaganda to ensure that the Serbian people are informed fully and in time about the political and security situation in the municipality and beyond." You -- you agree that that task was allocated to four people, including you?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you carry it out?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the task in itself was useless, stepping up information and propaganda activity. We had no means for doing that. And an alternative would have been for the four of us to knock on people's doors where Serbs used to live and we would have had to explain to people that security situation. So we did not do that. But this task was to be carried out to a certain extent later on in the month of March and it was carried out by myself and Zarko Djurovic on our own and it was at the point when the situation had already reached a point of crisis. But as far as I can remember, this task number 8 had not been carried out by us at that stage, because we did not have any conditions to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At page 4 of Tuesday's transcript, you said -- you commented, as you have done this morning, that something had seemed to be missing from the document at tab 13. I'm not going over that, because you've explained what you've said it was. But you also said, line 12: "I don't quite understand why such a serious large-scale plan is being discussed at the Crisis Staff meeting of a local commune." Is -- is that -- well, first of all, is -- is it -- can you confirm that is what you meant to say?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think this is a misunderstanding which has been cleared up already. There was a Municipal Crisis Staff here and the meeting was simply taking place at the premises of the local community Lukavica. So it was a higher level. It was a Municipal Crisis Staff simply holding a meeting in the premises of that local community in Lukavica. And what is missing here is -- the way I see it, I think there is something missing in the document of the 23rd of December. There seems to be something hanging in the air, as it were. We would need something else, such as, for example, the report from the working parties, what did they do, did they do anything indeed according to the distribution of duties and what was the commander of the Crisis Staff to whom this report had to be submitted, because the signature of that commander is missing here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Neskovic, it appears clear from your evidence, but take the opportunity to correct it if you need it, but in your view something was missing from both documents, both the 23rd December document at page -- at tab 12, and also from the 29th of January document, at tab 13. That -- you said at line 11, page 4: "And as in the case of the previous document there, is something that seems to be missing in this document too." So this is your opportunity to correct that, but you're -- which I'm inviting you to do, if it needs correction. But what we have as it stands is that your -- your evidence that there was something missing from both documents. Did you wish to correct that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only express my own personal opinion here. I believe that the explanation for these things that are missing are probably -- is probably due to the fact that the leadership presumably wanted to meet their obligations with regard to Variant A and B and wanted to be seen by Mr. Karadzic to be complying but that in practice they acted differently and they basically paid lip service to this but did not do what they were told to do in quite the same way as it was indicated in this Variant A and B. I don't know whether it was indicative of some kind of obstructionism, but I can conclude that this leadership was not really in the mood to implement A and B, and, on the other hand, they had to be seen to be doing something in a purely formal way, in order to be able to be seen as towing the party line. And so I don't really have an explanation for this. There are no reports as to who did what, but these are the results. So that's the way I interpret this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Neskovic, can we take it that you couldn't remember yesterday, you still can't remember who was the head of the Crisis Staff in January 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Formally speaking, it would have had to be the president of the Executive Committee of the Municipality; that is to say, Zarko Djurovic in this case. And I really don't know why his signature is missing as well, whether he was avoiding it. Djurovic did indeed avoid implementing Variant A and B, even though he never opposed anything openly. He tried to strike some kind of balance, to be kind of obedient and to be seen as being obedient and, on the other hand, he tried to do as little as possible or nothing at all. So that's why understand that he probably wouldn't have wanted to sign anything like this. He was trying to implement -- avoid implementing Variant A and B. And in the end, by the beginning of the war he actually fled the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You described an occasion, and you said it was the only occasion, on which Dr. Karadzic and Mr. Krajisnik came to a meeting at your municipality in connection with the problem over Mr. Djurovic, and you said - this is page 7 of yesterday's transcript, line 5 - "So I think they managed to replace Djurovic in the conflict, and when Karadzic and Krajisnik arrived, I think that the two of them managed to calm the situation down, and that meant maintaining the status quo." Would it be correct, Mr. Neskovic, that in saying that the two of them managed to calm the situation down, the person who was instrumental most in calming the situation down was Mr. Krajisnik, rather than Dr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Mr. Djurovic, when he felt that the tension was mounting and that his job was in jeopardy, I think he went to see Mr. Krajisnik. As to whether anyone else was present at that meeting, such as Karadzic or anyone else, I don't know because I wasn't present. But whatever happened, both of them came over and both of them tried to calm things down because calming things down would mean for the status quo to continue to exist and for him not to be replaced. Had they not come, he would have been sacked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked - it's also page 7 of that transcript - Mr. Tieger said: "And I understand from your testimony that Dr. Karadzic and Mr. Krajisnik intervened in the manner you just described. My question was a little bit different, and that's whether or not Mr. Djurovic reached out to or himself sought the assistance of Mr. Krajisnik or Dr. Karadzic in order to get them to intervene in this manner." And your answer was: "As far as I know, before that meeting was held, he" -- and that would be Mr. Djurovic -- "contacted Mr. Krajisnik, his office, and the Assembly - and I don't know whether Karadzic attended that meeting, too - as far as I know, he" -- that would have been Djurovic -- "contacted him" -- that clearly, you meant Krajisnik -- "to obtain assistance from him," Krajisnik, "before that meeting was held." Mr. Neskovic, I put it to you, you just do not know that, do you?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me repeat that I do know that Djurovic went to see Mr. Krajisnik at his office. I don't know exactly what the details of their conversation were and I don't know who else was present other than the two of them. I know that that critical meeting was attended by Mr. Krajisnik and Mr. Karadzic and they tried to calm things down in a way that I've described. I certainly do not know what exactly was said, what words were uttered in Mr. Krajisnik's office, because I wasn't present during the meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You talked about a huge meeting - this is at page 19 of the transcript - "a huge meeting, organised at the Presidencies of the Energoinvest company at Lukavica, chaired by the government commissioner for new Sarajevo, Mr. Milimir Mucibabic." And you said, "Different groups attended that meeting" -- I'm summarising: Armed forces, soldiers, Municipal Crisis Staff, government, et cetera, it comes across in the transcript, as though -- "it was a varied meeting with a picturesque attendance, and it was rather difficult." Mr. Neskovic, have I got it right that that meeting was in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in July, July 1992. Crisis Staff was no longer in existence. It ceased to exist on the 10th of June, 1992. And as of that date, he no longer existed. So according to my recollection, it could be either the end of June or the beginning of July. I rather think it was in July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Neskovic, you said - this is line 8, page 19 - "A great deal of criticism was voiced in the direction of the leadership at Pale, and the Presidency in the sense -- when we said 'Presidency,' what we meant was Karadzic, Krajisnik, Plavsic and Koljevic, and a great deal of dissatisfaction was discussed with regard to the government, as well." Now, Mr. Neskovic, do you remember who was the head of the government at that time?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Branko Djeric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, I'm -- just I said yesterday that I would do some of the bookkeeping. If we would not strictly apply the 60-per cent guidance, then -- if we would go well beyond that, you would have another 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And, Mr. Krajisnik, just for you to know, you will be granted not more than 15 minutes for additional questions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's synchronise watches, Mr. Neskovic. What were the key points of dissatisfaction expressed with regard to the government? Do you remember? My time's running out, Mr. Neskovic. I want you to think about your answers, but please also answer them as briskly as you can manage consistently with thinking about them.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main reason was that the Serb leadership had fled to Pale and they left the people behind in that area at the mercy of the events of war. And people tended to say if Alija Izetbegovic is happy to be with his people in Sarajevo, why can't the Serb leadership be with their nation here at Lukavica? So they were continued to have fled for their own safety. That it was first reason. And the second reason which was much more serious and much more dangerous, as it were: Rumours had started that -- to the effect that Sarajevo at the final moments of the war would be a bargaining chip and that it would have been left to the Bosniaks. And there were, however, 180.000 Serbs in the area and they were extremely shocked and frustrated even at the mention of such a possibility. And there were other problems as well. Quite simply that the leadership at Pale went there for their own safety and comfort that they cut themselves off from the day-to-day problems of the population. They left the people in a lurch and that their actions were slightly irresponsible and people were very dissatisfied and very angry and obviously each group had their own grievances as well. So that's what I remember about the reasons for all that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So so far as the government was concerned, there was a feeling that -- was there, that Mr. Djeric and his colleagues in the government bore a heavy responsibility which they were not satisfactorily discharging? Was that the feeling?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dissatisfaction was first and foremost with regard to the Presidency; that is to say, carriage, Krajisnik, Koljevic, and Plavsic. Not so much with regard to Djeric because government commissioner Mr. Mucibabic was present in that meeting and in some kind -- way he was there on behalf of the government and for the most part he was on our side, if I may use this expression. He was with us in expressing this dissatisfaction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Neskovic, are you therefore saying that you wish to downgrade what you said yesterday when you said specifically "a great deal of dissatisfaction was expressed with regard to the government as well"? Are you wanting to downgrade that from "a great deal of dissatisfaction"?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The government -- no. I'm sticking to my original statement, in exactly the same way as I said yesterday. I simply said that there was this positive gesture on the part of Mr. Mucibabic, who came there as somebody from the government. But I am not expressing a positive view of the entire government because they, too, fled to Jahorina to a comfy hotel far away from problems and difficulties of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Neskovic. The -- you talked about Professor Mucibabic fleeing from the area. What happened to him in the end? Is he alive and well now?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was scared of the consequences and he fled to Pristina, where he was a professor, and then he went on to Belgrade and he's a university lecturer in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Neskovic, Mr. Stewart didn't ask you for the itinerary but whether he's safe and well. That's what Mr. Stewart would like to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. He's fine, in excellent health.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm delighted to hear it, Mr. Neskovic. The -- you -- you've never had any personal fear of Mr. Krajisnik, have you, Mr. Neskovic?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't afraid of Krajisnik. I took notice of him. But my activities and his activities did not mean that we ever had to cross paths. I was involved with party activities and he did the Assembly work. So our relationship was neither good nor bad. We did not have many contacts. So what I can say is that yes, we did not have a relationship that was either good or bad. I wasn't in touch with him very often. I had no special need to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At page 42 of yesterday's transcript, you said - this is line 8 - "And also you've heard the fact that the top leadership at Pale was told about Batko by Biljana Plavsic and it never yielded any results." Now, as a matter of fact, Mr. Neskovic, I have been unable to find in the transcript where the Trial Chamber had heard the fact that the top leadership at Pale had been told about Batko by Biljana Plavsic. What I was able to find was a reference to Biljana Plavsic knowing something about that. But therefore in order to clear this up, I want to put this to you: Do you know anything to support the proposition that Mr. Krajisnik was told about Batko by Biljana Plavsic?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As to the relationship between Batko and Biljana Plavsic, I can only say what I read in her book. She found out about him. She visited the municipality to try and glean some extra information about him. She was told many horrible things. Then she went to Pale, and I think she went -- she went and got in touch with Momcilo Mandic and Mico Stanisic straight away because one was the justice minister and the other was the police chief, and so she felt that they would be the best-placed people to look into this issue. As to whether she informed the rest of the Presidency with Koljevic, Krajisnik, and Karadzic, whether they discussed Batko together, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The -- Mr. Neskovic, you were interviewed over two days on behalf of the -- or by representatives of the offices of the Prosecution, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was expressly made clear to you at the very beginning of that interview that you were regarded by them as in -- within the definition - that's at page 1 - it says - you needn't look at it. I'm just reading verbatim - "Based on the information" -- it's Finn Tollefsen talking. "Based on the information the Tribunal has, we consider that you fall into the definition of a suspect" -- or "the suspect," it says -- "under the Statute of the Tribunal. Therefore, before we ask you further questions we are required to advise you of certain rights that you have. Do you understand?" And you said: "Yes." Mr. Neskovic, at the time that that interview began, as succinctly as you can, what did you understand to be the particular matters which put you in the category of a suspect?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, given the interview -- Mr. Margetts interviewed me. He informed me of the rules. He said that I had the right to speak or to remain silent. He said I had the right to a lawyer and that they could pay for a lawyer if I had no resources and that I had the right to an interpreter, et cetera. I said there were no problems, that we could have this interview. They then told me that I fell in the category of a suspect --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Neskovic, excuse me. That is not my question at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I -- Mr. Stewart wants to know from you, Mr. Neskovic, what you thought could be the basis for the Office of the Prosecution to consider you to be a suspect.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I could not work that out because Mr. Margetts had told me that I could be held responsible for certain things. That's all I was told.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I couldn't guess what he meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question is not what Mr. Margetts told you but when they told you "you, in our view, are a suspect," what you thought could be the basis of a suspicion against you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I believed that I was innocent, that there were no grounds for suspecting me, and I wasn't afraid of any documents or of any questions. I quite simply believed that there were no grounds upon which I could be considered to be guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Neskovic, that does not answer my question. You -- you assert your belief - I make no comment - you assert your belief that there were no grounds, but you acknowledge that you were being interviewed as someone within the definition of a suspect in the eyes of the Prosecution. Mr. Neskovic, are you saying that you had not the faintest idea what matters and what activities or inactivities on your part might have put you into that category in the eyes of the Prosecutors?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't the faintest idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you didn't ask, then, for any particulars or any indication from the Prosecutors or anybody else as to what it was that put you in that category? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't ask them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there you were, Mr. Neskovic -- let's get it straight -- being interviewed as a suspect, no idea why. You make no inquiry why. You decline the opportunity of having any legal assistance, and you go ahead with the interview. Is -- is that -- I just want to get it clear. If that is your position, please just confirm that that is your position.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I didn't ask them any questions. I quite simply went ahead with the interview.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it still your position that you still don't have any idea what it is that put you in the category, in the eyes of the Prosecutors, of a suspect?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is still my position.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stewart. Mr. Krajisnik, do you have any questions for Mr. Neskovic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, have I understood you correctly? Did you say that I would only have 15 minutes to put questions to this witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll first listen to your -- your time is limited to 15 minutes at this moment. As you know, it is the experiment of the Chamber was not to have two cross-examinations but a cross-examination and additional questions by you. So clearly select what you find most important.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Cross-examined by Mr. Krajisnik:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Neskovic.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would just like to put a few questions to you. Firstly, you said that Mr. Karadzic proposed me as a president of the Assembly. In the course of your interview with the Prosecution, you went into more details. Could you please elaborate on how I was proposed as president of the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Karadzic insisted on Krajisnik being the president of the Assembly and he told us that he had spoken to you on a number of occasions and that you resisted the idea. You said that you were involved in agriculture, that you didn't want such a position, et cetera. So Karadzic said that he was trying to persuade you to accept the position, and in the end you accepted to assume the position. As far as I can remember, these are the explanations that were provided by Radovan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have to pause briefly for the sake of the interpretation. Who proposed Mr. Trbojevic as a candidate? Can you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't remember. All I know is that Trbojevic prepared a sort of celebration one evening together with his wife to celebrate his appointment and in the morning the situation had completely changed and he was no longer a candidate for that post. I was one of the guests at that celebration, but as to who proposed him as a candidate, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This all took place in 1990; is that correct? After the elections?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the elections.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who proposed the other candidates, the ministers, et cetera, who were from the Serbian Democratic Party within the authorities of Bosnia and Herzegovina? Please pause briefly before you answer the question.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, Karadzic proposed them. Perhaps he did that in a restaurant in Kula. There were eight ministers representing the SDS and only one gentleman, Ostojic, was an active party member. The others were there for other reasons. They weren't prominent members of the SDS. As far as I know, Karadzic proposed them in the Kula restaurant. As to whether you were involved in that matter with him, I do not know, because I was not present in the Kula restaurant when they compiled those lists.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have another question for you now. When candidates were proposed for members of the Presidency, when a founding committee was established, when a list of deputies was compiled, at that time, as far as you know, was I close to Karadzic? Was I an acquaintance of Karadzic's?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know, you have been acquainted with Karadzic since before the war. You knew each other privately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your answer is yes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you provide a logical explanation as to why Karadzic didn't Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. then suggest that Krajisnik should be a member of the Presidency? Could you provide a reason for which I was not a member of the founding committee if I was close to Karadzic and if that was the reason for which Karadzic proposed me as president of the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I believe that Karadzic told a group to compile a list of candidates for the electoral unit in Sarajevo. I think you were the last person on that list, so you only barely managed to get through and Plavsic and Koljevic entered the Presidency and Koljevic [as interpreted] too. I don't know how this was done though, but I think it went through the Political Council. I think it was done through the Political Council.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the registrar just provide document number 4, please. -- I apologise, not number 4 but number 5. It's document number 5. I don't think this is the right one. It's a handwritten note. I can provide Mr. -- I can provide the gentleman with my copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please give us the last three digits of the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I didn't have my headphones on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 0205269, minutes from the session of the Executive Committee. It's the 7th Session of the Executive Committee or Executive Board. SA038957.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think there might be a digit missing. It's 02052469, is the first page of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's in front of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just have a look at the note from the Executive Committee. Could you have a look at the last page of that document. Have a look at item 5. You can see that the Executive Board was informed of the establishment of a new body. Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps you have forgotten this. You said the Executive Board did not know what Novi Privrednik was. Could you please read that through to yourself and you attended the meeting.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a look at the section that concerns Novi Privrednik, or New Privrednik. Here it says that this should have been --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, where exactly are we? What page, as far -- I only need the last three digits of the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 8961. SA 03 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 8961.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Now you are reading from number 5; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Item 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please read slowly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try to read it slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "The Executive Board was informed of the fact that the New Privrednik was founded and after the action taken to date as well as of the subsequent tasks that had to be carried out. In this respect, the conclusion was reached that it was necessary to support the founding Assembly of the company as soon as possible and to start implementing decisions taken by the Assembly. The party, as a -- the body that founded this company, cannot have any shares for the simple reason that as a political organisation it cannot make any profit. The conclusion was that the shares should immediately be put on the market and a shareholders' meeting should be held, after which the party as a political organisation would distance itself, in inverted commas, from the company. It is necessary to immediately send a letter to inform the Municipal Boards of the fact that the New Privrednik has been established, inform them of the importance to have company and tell them that shareholders are being sought and that 10.000 dinars should be invested as shares." And this was at a meeting at which Mr. Milivojevic explained what Novi Privrednik or New Privrednik was. Do you remember that meeting in the reports?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, the last lines: "And this was at a meeting at which Mr. Milivojevic explained what" -- that is not the text, that is comment, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This relates to a document that comes before this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not in this document. Then you should have refrained from putting it to the witness. I invited you to read it and you can put questions to the witness. However, you cannot explain to the witness what happened at that meeting. Please move to your next question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I read out this part and I put a question to the witness. Perhaps there's a misunderstanding. I asked him whether he remembered this record when he was informed of the New Privrednik. I wanted to mention that there was a meeting at which all of this was mentioned. Everything that's contained in this document was also mentioned.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the minutes, but I now see that minutes were taken and there was an Executive Board that I attended. To this very day, I don't know what Novi Privrednik is. Here it says that "The party established the Privrednik company and that the party was selling shares for private individuals through parties and they should pay 10.000 dinars for the shares. They said they would take their distance from the company, in inverted commas. Percentages were also mentioned." So as far as I know, as a member of the Executive Board, at the time I did not know what Novi Privrednik was nor do I know what Novi Privrednik is today. I also don't know what sort of transactions it was involved in. I don't know what sort of resources it had.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Neskovic, at the time, why didn't you ask for any explanations from Mr. Dukic? Because there's a document here and it says that you were present at a meeting, and this is a document that is on the first page of document number 5.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Dukic as the president of the Executive Committee was responsible for business and for commercial matters. He was involved in his own affairs. I wasn't involved in business of any kind. I was involved in the party. Novi Privrednik or New Privrednik didn't interest me much, because it wasn't my intention to become a shareholder and I didn't try to obtain much information about Privrednik. I wasn't very interested in this. It was Dukic's responsibility to establish a link between Privrednik and the party. He was responsible for such business in the party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please have a look at document number 6.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document please be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This will be your last question. Mr. Krajisnik, I might have been too quick where I ignored that what seemed to me to be a comment finally ended up being a question, so therefore I was perhaps too quick. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, while it's being distributed, if Mr. Krajisnik could indicate the title of that document in addition to the number in which it was distributed, it would make it easier to find.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Krajisnik, do you have -- could you give us a clue on --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I apologise. It's document -- one of the pages is from Grkovic's diary. SA0403905.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that in evidence already or is that ...?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I apologise. I said 6. It's SA 023626. It's the 6th Session of the Executive Board, of the SDS Executive Board. 023623. The page is SA023623 and it's interesting. It's the last page or the penultimate page, for Mr. Neskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's item 6. With Your Honours' leave, I would like to read this page. It's not much. And I will then have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so, Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The text on page 6 is as follows: "It has been decided that there should be assistance for filming a film on refugees and 100.000 dinars will be provided. It has been decided that assistance should be provided to the Municipal Board of the SDS in Tesanj. They will be given 50.000 dinars. It has been decided that in accordance with what is possible, all municipal SDS boards in Bia [phoen] should be provided with assistance that they need. It has also been decided that the league for fighting epilepsy should be assisted and they should be provided with 50.000 dinars. It has been decided that the municipal SDS board in Stari Grad, Sarajevo should contact the town board of the Sarajevo SDS for assistance. It has been concluded that the requests submitted by Mr. Radomir Neskovic that concerns regulating the status of his work in the BSDS and that he should be granted a loan of 350.000 dinars to construct a house. This request should be submitted to the Commission for Personnel and Organisational Matters. They will consider this request. It has been decided that oil and oil products should be provided more sparingly, more economically. The president of the Executive Committee of Bia [phoen] should send a letter to the director of Jugopetrol in Belgrade." My question is as follows: In the course of the examination, in the course of your testimony, did you see the document about the contract between the SDS and Boxit, between Karadzic and Djukic?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I can show you this document, but you commented on the document in your testimony.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While you're looking for it, could I just say something? The problem was that Mr. Karadzic did not have the right to sign financial contracts in the party. Those who had such a right were Mr. Dukic and myself. And then an odd situation occurred, because the party had to sign some kind of a contract with Boxit and the director of Boxit was Mr. Dukic, whereas the representative of the Executive Board was Mr. Dukic. So the situation was a little odd because this gentleman would have had to sign a contract with himself. In order to avoid such a situation, Mr. Karadzic probably signed the contract, although Karadzic did not have the right to sign such financial documents. He wasn't someone who had the right to sign such documents. He wasn't registered in the court that authorised such matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we put the document on the ELMO. The witness can see it on his screen.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a document that the Prosecution has used on a number of occasions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is this in evidence already? I don't know what it is; therefore, I wanted it to be put on the ELMO if there are no copies. Is there any -- please put it on the ELMO, yes. And take care that the witness sees -- yes. Okay. Please put a question to the witness, Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a contract which is based on the decision taken by the Executive Board according to which one should sign a contract with Jugopetrol and Karadzic and Mr. Dukic signed it. It is a contract between the SDS and the Boxit company and Mr. Dukic was its director. Do you remember this contract?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But what was signed on the contract and what's stated in the decision of the Executive Committee doesn't completely tally. The conclusion says: "In order to provide oil more sparingly, the director of the Jugopetrol company should be contacted by post." It doesn't say that something has to be signed with -- that a contract has to be signed with Boxit. It's something that can be explained with difficulty because we have a situation in which Mr. Rajko Dukic signed a contract with himself, because he was the president of the Executive Board and, on the other hand, he was the director of the Boxit company. And since it's impossible to sign a contract with oneself, Karadzic signed the contract. But once again, I'll repeat that Karadzic didn't have the right to sign such a financial document. Dukic had this right. We had been registered at the court as individuals who were authorised to sign such documents. So this involves financial acrobatics and I was not involved in this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Neskovic, Mr. Dukic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is your last question, Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRAJISNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this contract, Mr. Dukic, as the director of the company, assumes the responsibility of obtaining oil from Jugopetrol in Belgrade because that was a privilege that Karadzic and Dukic had. That was their prerogative. And they said that they would then provide the party with 3 per cent. In your opinion, is such a contract completely legal?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. Not because Mr. Dukic was the president of the Executive Board and if he should have signed a contract with some company, it should have been with some other company, not with the Boxit company. The contract should have been a lot clearer so that the party could then control the percentages involved, the prices involved. When you have such a large-scale transaction, well, the contract is very short, in fact, given the size of the transaction. And I believe that this contract is not quite regular.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to thank Your Honours and the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Tieger, I'm looking at the clock. How much time would you need for re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I've got, I believe -- well, I would say 10 to 15 minutes, Your Honour, and because a couple of the documents are involved. But there is an issue with -- with setting up the courtroom for the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So I'm prepared to proceed or we can proceed afterwards with some accommodation by the Defence or the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then for setting up the protective measures, we invite you to continue at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Re-examined by Mr. Tieger:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Neskovic, I have a few questions for you. First, a quite minor matter, I think. In connection with a portion of yesterday's transcript that Mr. Stewart asked you about, you were talking at that point about Mr. Djurovic contacting Mr. Krajisnik. And I'm just wondering if there's a -- a mistranslation or mispronunciation in the English transcript we received. The answer was, as written in the transcript: "As far as I know, before that meeting was held, he contacted Krajisnik, his office, and the Assembly," the transcript reads. And I wanted to know if you said that he contacted Krajisnik in his office in the Assembly.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Next you were asked yesterday at page 69, I believe, some questions about liaising with the government, and you had said that "The liaison with the Republika Srpska government always went through Karadzic and Krajisnik, at all times, in all the relevant years." Then you were asked about liaising with the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina as well, and you said at some point - this is page 69, as I say - "I am also thinking about the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina," and then you continued, "in which there were eight Serbian ministers." And later on you were asked a question - that's at the bottom of page 69 - about whether -- or about high-level contacts between the Bosnian Serbs and the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina going through Dr. Karadzic and Mr. Krajisnik, and your answer was yes. I simply wanted to ask you: In connection with your comment about liaising with the government of Republika Srpska and your mention of the eight Serbian ministers, did liaising with the Serbian ministers and the Serbian officials within the Bosnia and Herzegovina government before the split, was that also something that went through Karadzic and Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I wonder could -- could I have -- because it may be that there's a discrepancy in numbers here. Could I have more specifically the transcript reference there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, could you assist Mr. Stewart?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: All of the references I made were on page -- I'm sorry, either the bottom of page 68 or the top of page 69 on the -- what is now the draft official transcript. That would begin, for Mr. Stewart's benefit, I would think -- I mean, he apparently has a version that goes farther on. So if he began with the -- he says -- the Court says to him: "Perhaps if you'd very much limit yourself." Mr. Stewart says: "Thank you, Your Honour." He begins a question: "Thank you, Mr. Neskovic." And the beginning of my references are contained in the answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm still -- I'm still struggling. A phrase like -- perhaps "if you very much limit yourself" is far from unique, but some of the others -- I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If you looked at: "So, Mr. Neskovic, you're talking about Mr. Ostojic." That's one reference. That's a question on that page. There's also a question that begins above that: "Can I just say, Mr. Neskovic, you're being doubly enthusiastic." I ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I don't know whether I'm -- I'm sorry, I don't know whether I'm pages apart here. That's the trouble. It's a problem for Mr. Tieger as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the -- in the electronic version, it's page 68, line 10, where it says: "So, Mr. Neskovic, you are talking about Mr. Ostojic."

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I've got it, Your Honour. I'm on page 72. We're three pages apart. I don't know how that happens but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, neither do we.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: One day, perhaps over the next month or two, three, four, we might sort that out. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: After all that, perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much. I have it now. I beg your pardon. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If I could simply ask Mr. Neskovic the question again in a simple way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Neskovic, did the liaison with the Serbian officials, the -- in the Bosnian-Herzegovinian government, the ministers and so on, go through Dr. Karadzic or Mr. Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was quite usual for them to communicate with Mr. Krajisnik, Karadzic, Koljevic, and Mrs. Plavsic, so that they did talk to one another. And just one correction with regard to Mr. Ostojic. I only mentioned his name within the overall context, as him being the only prominent member who was not an SDS, whereas the others got into government in different ways. And then, of course, they had the same sorts of contacts between Muslims with their own parties and the Croats with their own and the Serb leadership had contacts with their own ministers. Sometimes the ministers initiated those contacts; sometimes the other way around. Basically those contacts existed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You were also asked about instructions from the leadership of the SDS to municipalities. May I ask you, please, to turn to tab 3 of the binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Tab 3, I believe, is already in evidence, although I don't have the number in front of me. It's a document dated August 15th,1991 to all SDS boards signed by Dr. Karadzic as Serbian president of the -- government of BH entitled "Operating instructions obligatory for everybody."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the instructions and activities reflected in that document?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I could also ask you to turn quickly to tab 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, is -- is Mr. Tieger re-examining or is he plugging gaps which he's now identified on review in his examination-in-chief? Because I don't recall asking anything at all about tab 3. And it's -- everything in a sense is related to everything else in this case, but that's not the guideline for re-examination. So far Mr. Tieger has --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'd be happy to respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Tieger's previous question simply went over exactly the same ground and elicited the same answer has I have not challenged, so that didn't really advance the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's a simple response.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could Mr. -- yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I attempted to conduct an efficient examination-in-chief as possible so I did not go to those documents. In cross-examination, Mr. Stewart asked whether Variant A and B it was -- the only such instruction issued by the party to the Municipal Board.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So I'm obliged -- this is a very efficient way of coming back to that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may put the question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Neskovic, looking quickly at tab 4, and that document, which is a session of the Club of Deputies of the SDS. On the second-to-last page of the English - and I think it's perhaps on page -- the page number that ends 506, with the -- with the listing at the top 506 in your version - Dr. Karadzic says: "I have decided to impose a state of emergency in the party." This Court has already received in evidence telegrams to and from municipalities reflecting a state of emergency that was introduced on October 18th. My question is: Were you familiar with that state of emergency imposed by Dr. Karadzic on October 18th?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of that state of emergency. And since I was a member of the Executive Board, I should have known. And I really don't know what it meant and -- by virtue of what it was any different from the normal routine functioning of the party. If I may, with regard to those guidelines of the 15th of August, this is a public document in order to start to implement the program in the statute of the Assembly of the 12th of July, that is to say, to step up work within the party in that respect. And then so these guidelines are being provided in order to be able to intensify all that activity. And as to the October thing and the extraordinary situation, I really don't know. I have no idea what Karadzic meant by that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. And could I ask you to turn quickly to tab 30.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That needs to be marked next in order, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Tab 30 would be Prosecution Exhibit P915, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Neskovic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: P915 reflect the minutes of the Municipal Board of Novo Sarajevo SDS. If I could ask you to turn -- that was held, by the way, on October 29th, 1991. And if I could ask you to look quickly at item 2, the second entry, which indicates that "Ranko Jugovic informed that the state of emergency had been declared in the party."

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's clear to me now. I think it is the activities of the party with regard to the referendum, and I think that the party was supposed to engage in a sustainable effort in order to promote vote in favour of staying within the former Yugoslavia on the part of the Serb people. So I think that's what they called an emergency, in order to be able to impose a bit more discipline. So it is clear to me now. What they meant was the maximum level of effort, the sustained effort, in organising the referendum for the Serbs in Bosnia and Herzegovina in the month of November. So all the activities that had to do with that upcoming referendum, that's what I gather it must mean on the basis of these minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that the document in tab 3, the August 15th instructions and the imposition of the state of emergency by Dr. Karadzic on October 18th, reflect ways through which the party leadership issued directives and instructions to lower-ranking SDS bodies?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I don't know -- what sort of question is that? It -- it is -- they are what they are, really. And -- and what possibly can an answer to that question add to any knowledge of the Trial Chamber in relation to this matter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, according to Mr. Stewart, the document speaks for itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, if the document speaks for itself in exactly the way I asked the question, I'm more than satisfied.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I didn't say that, Your Honour. The document speaks for itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's precisely the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: No, it's not. Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you may ask the question, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger is not entitled to put his own interpretation to the witness in that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, could you formulate your question in a way that clarifies the content of the -- the meaning of the document, without giving the answer in the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the document in August -- the document issued on August 15th and sent to all Municipal Boards a mandatory instruction that was required to be implemented?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It was addressed to all the Municipal Boards, Your Honour. We -- I don't believe we have evidence that it was sent to all the Municipal Boards.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to try and answer. This August document, in my view, represents a legal and regular party procedure within the framework of which the president of the party on the strength of his authority instructs municipal bodies to step up their activities based on the programme which was approved on the 12th of July and since the organisation structure of the party had changed after the 15th of July, those instructions were to the effect for the new -- that the new membership should adjust to this new organisation structure and that it should become fully operational. So that's the way I read it, as a normal, regular, usual way of functioning. And after the 12th of July, as I said, the structure had changed and so they have to adjust to that change. And as to the second document, it is about an emergency situation -- or I would rather tend to call it party activities in the course of a rather special period of time; that is to say, when the referendum was being organised. And so that's why they keep using the term of an emergency. In other words, they are asking every single member and every part of the party to do their utmost in order to make sure that as many Serbs as possible vote in the referendum and that they should engage in party propaganda. And so that was their preparation for the upcoming referendum. And so I really fail to see any link between the two documents. The first one is a party routine kind of document, whereas the second one is about the functioning to have party in relation to a specific event, in this case a referendum. So it was a kind of an extraordinarily active period for the party.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah, I have -- I have one more question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm looking at the clock and I'm also -- I would have to look back, but you said that you thought 10 minutes would do approximately --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, I also did indicate that there were a number of documents and I tried to move through as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm willing to, Your Honour, ask the last question under the conditions -- we've done that before, I know -- under the protective measures conditions then simply release the transcript in the normal fashion. If that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart is looking puzzled. The idea is we're going to impose some --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That we work under the conditions of face and voice distortion and then immediately release that to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, we could maybe get through the question and answer in the time that we're debating the procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems that Mr. -- Mr. Tieger, you said approximately 10 minutes and you said a few documents. Let's finish within the next three minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm referring now to the transcript the day before yesterday. And in my version, approximately -- begins approximately the series of questions around page 22 but the -- and the specific portion I'm referring to is at page 25 of my version. The reference -- phrase, I guess, would be -- the witness says: "Could you please clarify something." And the beginning of my question is: "Well, I understood you to say."

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I have it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Neskovic, the day before yesterday I had asked you some questions about who made decisions or established policy and who enforced policy within the party after people assumed positions within government, after the elections. And you explained that and identified certain people in your answer. Today Mr. Stewart asked you some questions about Mr. -- and let me just say -- before I say that, and you identified Mr. Krajisnik as being one of those persons. Today Mr. Stewart asked you about who had executive power or what executive authority Mr. Krajisnik had within the party. I just want to ask you a question distinguishing between formal Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. executive authority and the reality of who had power within the party. Today you said that Mr. Karadzic and Mr. Krajisnik were supreme authorities in the party. When you referred, then, yesterday to people who had the power to make decisions and enforce decisions within the party, would Mr. -- would Dr. Karadzic and Mr. Krajisnik have been the two top people to do that?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That's a bit more than leading, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No, I think it's clarifying, given all the --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, leading often is clarifying and clarifying is often leading but it's the leading bit which is objectionable, not the clarifying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you have to rank those with most power in the party, what would your ranking be from the top down to the bottom? Well, first three, four, five.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the very top, Mr. Karadzic. At the Main Board, well, there were elections and it was a collective body and it was 45 people. But within the party --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm talking about persons. Who would be next? Who would be number two most powerful in the party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The second one within the party itself? Velibor Ostojic maybe, Rajko Dukic. And for a certain period of time, Jovo Mijatovic from Zvornik and Bozo Vucurevic and I think Vojo Kupresanin as well. Well, basically the power within the party was in the hands of those who were members of the central party bodies and structures and at the same time they had positions of authority in their own municipalities. They had large and powerful constituencies. And another person who played another important role within the party was Aleksa Buha and -- and I can't remember. And the late Jovo Jovanovic, who was the head of the Municipal Board for Sarajevo. I don't know. Some others. Is this enough or do you want me to go on?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it's at least a surprising in view of -- of the interview that until now -- no, let me -- I would like to -- I'll leave it to Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you told us about -- and today I think you mentioned it as well, the extent to which the party was -- I think you used the word "marginalised" after the assumption of power in positions of government following the elections by SDS officials. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you told us about the people who held the most power in the party after that time, the people with whom Dr. Karadzic worked most closely with and the people who with him made --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Tieger -- perhaps, Mr. Tieger, let's put it to the witness right away. In your answer, you did not mention Mr. Krajisnik. In your interview, the following question was put to you: "In relation to the implementation of instructions" --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: May I have a paragraph, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm referring to page 89.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- you said: "Who were the supreme authorities of the Serb movement." Is the Serb movement something else than the SDS party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely. The Serb movement and the Serb leadership and the leadership of the party are not one and the same thing. So maybe that's why my answer was a bit confusing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, then who were the supreme authorities of the Serb movement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The supreme authorities there would be Mr. Krajisnik and Mr. Karadzic and I would not be able to say who was the more important. I would say that they were equal in authority there and they were both number one and in a way they represented the top level of power, and then there was a void behind them, nothing at all, and then lagging somewhat behind was Koljevic, Plavsic, Maksimovic, and others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So that was the permanent leadership and the top people in power, because supreme power does not always tally with the positions -- formal positions with the party. They'd tally in the case of Mr. Karadzic. But I do apologise, Your Honours. I was a bit confused. Because the party structure is one thing. The Serb movement and the leaders of that movement is another thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were the policies of Dr. Karadzic and Mr. Krajisnik implemented through the party, through the Republika Srpska governmental structures or political structures or through both?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are many answers to that question. For the most part, through the Deputies' Club and the MPs basically, and through government ministers and -- and the MUP staff and officials. And then businessmen of -- of certain standing, heads of companies, et cetera. And also through the Serb Democratic Party wherever necessary, such as, for example, in the case of the referendum, because no other body other than the SDS could have done that, and so on occasion it was done through the structures of the Serb Democratic Party. But most policies were implemented through people in the government, whether they were in the joint structures of government of Bosnia and Herzegovina or in the Republika Srpska. And I believe that the Deputies Club played a very important role there and later on the Presidency. There were quite a few bodies. To be quite honest, I can't sometimes even tell one from the other because there were all sorts of Presidencies and changes to the Constitution and all that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm sure I've exhausted the Court's patience. I appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Any need for re-examination, Mr. Stewart? The Bench has no questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, in a sense the Bench is -- the Bench has put its questions, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No. No. We have -- yes. Well, if there's any need to put any further questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Excuse me one moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Triggered by re-examination. I do understand that Mr. Krajisnik would have -- we have four minutes left on the tape, so that ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, if you have any question at this moment, please put it to the witness or after Mr. Stewart has put his questions to the witness. We've got four minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, what I'm trying to do at the moment is just establish whether Mr. Krajisnik wishes to address the Trial Chamber or wishes to consult with me. May I just find out which of those it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. I have a question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It's nice and simple. Further cross-examination by Mr. Stewart:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Neskovic, you've talked a lot over the last few minutes about supreme authorities and so on. Can you give a single example that you can recall of Mr. Krajisnik issuing an order to anybody?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NESKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't present in any such situation when orders were formally issued.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the answer is no. I just want to make that clear. You added something at the end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. No further questions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we will have a break until 25 minutes past 1.00. And I'll start with one -- a couple of procedural issues which then will later have to be made public. They're all of a technical nature, but we have to deal with them today. So the parties should be prepared that that might take five minutes in the beginning. Mr. Neskovic, this concludes your testimony. I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and to answer the questions put by all the parties and to the Bench -- by the Bench. I wish you a safe trip home again. You are excused. We'll adjourn until -- and we'll deal with the exhibits at a later moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We cannot have a break for 20 minutes because we need half an hour to prepare for the next witness's protective measures, therefore we spend rather our time on the procedural issues. That might take us some 10 or 15 minutes. Whatever is left could be dealt with. And then we'll start with the next witness tomorrow morning. Mr. Margetts, it's not the way I had it in mind, but it is as it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I believe Mr. Gaynor has five minutes of matters he'd like to address as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we'll adjourn until 25 minutes past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The remaining minutes we'll spend on some procedural issues. First of all - and I'm specifically addressing you, Mr. Krajisnik - the Chamber received this morning a memo from the representative of the Registry. The Chamber was earlier already informed by yourself that no agreement had been reached as a result of the conversations you had with the representatives of the Registry, no results, part of it on the basis of the amount of money to be paid to investigators. We don't have to discuss this matter. The Chamber offered also on your request its good services to see whether any solution could be reached in the disagreement that existed between you and the Registry. This agreement has not been reached. The Chamber at that time considered that it should not move to decide on your request for self-representation at that time moment. Since now these talks have not been -- have not resulted in an agreement, the Chamber just wants to know build -- whether you still insist or whether you wish to represent yourself -- your wish to represent yourself is still standing, because if so, the Chamber will decide on the matter; if not, of course, there's nothing to decide any more. Could you tell the Chamber whether you still -- whether your request to represent yourself is still standing.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'd have to provide you with some detailed explanations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It wouldn't take very long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Mr. Krajisnik. The Chamber wants to know whether your request for self-representation still stands, because then the Chamber will decide. If it doesn't stand any more, there's nothing to decide. We do not want explanations. We just want to know what we have to do at this moment, and that is whether we have to give a decision, yes or no. If you say, "I need another three hours to -- to think about whether it's a yes or no," please do that, but we are not going into any discussions. We are not going into any negotiations. We are not going into any if this, then that, or who is to be blamed for the failure. It may be the Registry; it may be you. The Chamber just wants to know quite simply whether there's a request it has to decide upon or whether there's not.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't answer a question phrased in such a manner. That's why I would like to have at least half a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. The Chamber is not going to allow you to give further explanations. If you say, "I can't give an answer," it's quite simple. We -- you have requested to represent yourself. We did not give a decision until now because there were ongoing conversations with the Registry and perhaps with counsel as well. We offered our good services to promote them. We now just want to know, since we have been informed both by you and by the Registry that there's no agreement, so whether it has resulted in anything or not, yes or no, is another matter. We want to know whether this request is there to be decided upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, could I just observe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: -- that when Mr. Krajisnik said he would like to have at least half a minute, it wasn't clear whether he meant half a minute to say something or half a minute think about it. If he is requesting half a minute --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I thought half a minute of thinking. I thought to be half a minute to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. If it would be half a minute to think, Your Honour, might he be allowed a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I offered him --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour did indeed. And, of course, it may be that that's what he meant. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for drawing my attention to a possible misunderstanding. Mr. Krajisnik, did you want to think for 30 seconds or did you want to explain? Because we want a yes or a no.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to spend half a minute to say that we have agreed on certain issues. There is one matter that is outstanding and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, whether you agreed or everything, I did understand -- but if I'm wrong, it doesn't make any difference. If you have full agreement, fine; if you have 95 per cent of agreement, fine; if you have 60 per cent of agreement -- everything's fine. The only thing the Chamber wants to know is whether at this moment your request to represent yourself is still a pending request or whether it's -- it has to be struck off the record. That's the only thing the Chamber wants to know. And it's -- yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If only I could receive a response from the Registry, we can strike this item from the agenda. But I've done everything that was necessary in my contacts with the Registry. The task was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, you are again doing what you did before, that is, to start negotiating; if I would get this, then perhaps -- there's no way of that. The Chamber wants to know -- and if you don't give an answer, then there's no clear withdrawal. We offered our good services. We told you that we would wait to decide. So if you do not give a clear answer, a yes or a no, then it's quite clear; then the Chamber will give a decision. The Chamber will then give a decision on a matter which has been dealt with in this court in quite some depth, that is, the right to represent yourself or the circumstances or the case law, et cetera. It has been fully discussed. We then decided just to postpone our decision in order to give an opportunity to have further talks. Now we want to know whether that request is still pending, in which case the Chamber will give a decision.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could I have just half a minute? If you can't grant me half a minute, do as you please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It may have been clear to you, Mr. Krajisnik, that the Chamber wanted a yes or a no and that if it doesn't get it, it will take it to be that the matter is pending and the Chamber will then give a decision on your request. So therefore you are at this moment in a position to tell us whether it's still pending or not. If you don't do it, the Chamber will consider the matter still to be pending, since there's no clear withdrawal.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, could -- could I -- perhaps I'll try to be helpful, Your Honour. I certainly, with respect, endorse what the -- Your Honour has just said, but we're starting from the position where Mr. Krajisnik's initial position was clear, and if there is no unequivocal withdrawal, the position would be as -- as Your Honour says. On the assumption that this decision is clearly not going to be -- I take it it's not going to be given today that, it would be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I offered Mr. Krajisnik to think it over. If he needs a couple of hours, that would almost make impossible when we would decide and when that decision will be a full-reasoned decision or whether reasons will be given at a later stage is another matter. But I cannot, if that is -- today there will be no decision. That is one thing I can tell you for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, simply from a practical point of view --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It would appear to be this, Your Honour that, Your Honours will be proceeding on the basis there hasn't been an unequivocal withdrawal and therefore no withdrawal. But the position would be, one supposes, that any time up to the point where Your Honours actually deliver the decision if at any point before then Mr. Krajisnik did unequivocally withdraw his decision --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The matter would be moot.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: -- then the matter would be moot and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the matter would be moot and then --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So that Mr. Krajisnik understands that in effect the opportunity is at least there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.
