utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I make no comment whatsoever on his inclination to avail himself of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, that's clear. So if first thing Mr. Krajisnik would do when we enter court tomorrow morning is say it is a withdrawal, then of course the matter would be moot and he would not be surprised by a decision taken overnight.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, exactly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's clear. So that matter having been dealt with, yes, Mr. Krajisnik. Not on this issue, unless you want to give the Chamber yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we have a few other matters. The first one I'd like to deal with is about a Prosecution exhibit provisionally assigned with the number P566. Mr. Guy, I'm not -- Mr. Gaynor, I'm not -- I have been informed that we had not yet decided on P566 because it had to be resubmitted. I am now informed that you -- that the Defence through Ms. Loukas informed you that they would have no further objections against admission of P566 as you intend to submit it today.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. And I can submit it right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. Then, Mr. Usher, could you please -- that's P566.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, and P566.1, which is the B/C/S translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, would be the B/C/S translation. Since there were no other reasons that -- the Chamber, as always, relies on the correctness of the information provided by you, in this case, Mr. Gaynor, and therefore we'll admit P566 now in evidence. Then we have another matter. There has been a lot of confusion about the Zvornik contextual documents. They had been provided to the Defence and finally it turned out that they had not been provided to the Chamber. The Chamber then in some respects was a bit confused by the documents. Finally, they have been submitted again on the 7th of July -- no, not on the 7th of July. I think on the 4th of July. Then the Chamber still saw some technical problems. The Prosecution then responded that they did not understand what our technical problems were. Then the matter has been discussed by your case manager with one of the legal officers from the Chamber. This has led to a new corrected CD which has been submitted on the 12th of July. Usually, if an exhibit or at least contextual documents have been exhibited, usually a week is granted to the Defence to object or to further comment. They have been -- we have received it, and I take it Defence at the same day, on the 12th of July we have received this new CD. The Chamber established that practically all the technical problems had been solved. Normally the Defence would have until the 19th, but that's already behind us, so therefore if the Defence could please submit any objection by next Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This Friday, yes. I'm always making the mistakes what in English is this Friday and Dutch the next Friday. In some other languages it is the Friday of next week. That's good that I am corrected. Then we have -- there is resubmitted 92 bis material for the witnesses Zujo --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not -- it's not a very exciting matter. Perhaps we ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just out of caution, I wanted to check whether there were any protective measures involved. The -- there was a problem with the 92 bis materials in relation to the witnesses Zujo, Mesic, and Dobraca. The Chamber has deferred its decision on these three witnesses. The Office of the Prosecution has reviewed the material, and on the 15th of July the Prosecution has resubmitted the revised materials; therefore, the normal time to respond to that would be until the 22nd of July, and that's the date the Chamber would like to receive any objections, if there is -- are any.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm afraid that's not possible. I -- I'm not sure exactly when, but I -- I would have to double-check, but my clear recollection, though one can always -- memory place tricks -- is that we -- we did not have this material in our possession on the 15th of July, which was last Friday, wasn't it? It's -- it could be that -- that all that happens is these things slip over the weekends. But -- but, Your Honour, the -- it's not any particular complaint, but the whole point about this material was it was a fantastic mess. I'm not saying it's anybody's fault necessarily, but it was an incredible mess. And I've got a big pile of paper at home in relation to these people. And quite frankly, Your Honour, I do not have time to go through this -- this mess and check it all between now and Friday. I just don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The parties are invited to inform the Chamber by tomorrow morning at what time at least -- that's the first factual matter to be established -- at what time the Defence received this reorganised materials.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I say that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: -- just -- that -- of course, it's fair enough and we will check on our side, because I am working a little bit from memory and of course it may have got transmitted through. But even if it is assumed that we had it on Friday, in the particular circumstances, Your Honour, having this stuff landed on our plates at that point is just -- is just unrealistic to add that to everything else this week. Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was about -- these were the -- I think, the -- yes, these were mainly the exhumation reports and --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: They're that's correct, Your Honour. We've -- we've cut down the material involved. We've organised it so that it's much easier to navigate. We did file it on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I think the Registry, due to their own copying and distribution issues may not have provided a copy to the Defence on Friday. But it was formally filed on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it was mainly the Chamber that had problems with the material, rather than the Defence, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did we not at that time -- that the Chamber said --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- they said there were no objections against it. Perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That isn't the position, Your Honour. What had happened is it was many, many, weeks ago -- what had happened was that we'd -- we'd specifically said that it was just in so much of a tangle that we invited the Prosecution, invited through the Trial Chamber to go away and revisit it, which they've very helpfully gone, and that was understood. Your Honour, what Mr. Fergal says does absolutely match what I recall has happened over the last full couple of days. The first time I have been given - and I think I was given it immediately by my team, this material - was after the weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, what I intended to do was to have as clear as possible the information by tomorrow and, of course, whether what would that result in is another matter. But at least to -- not to discuss these factual issues where we can just listen, whereas you can speak to each other in a way and either agree or ask further information from the Registry or whatever to see whether you can agree on when it was provided to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd just like to say this. It seems -- I detect that what's happening is there is some notion, with respect, that, everything, everything, like this has all got to do be done by the 22nd of July. Your Honour there, are limits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mr. Stewart, it is five minutes to 2.00 and we are ten minutes over time. That's what the situation is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. Your Honour. In that case I'll sit down immediately because I'm as keen to get away as anybody, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore the Chamber would like to be informed about the date of receipt of these documents by the Defence. Let me just see what else was on my ... Yes. I just want to be -- to have confirmed in an open session: Did the Chamber understand you well, Mr. Gaynor, that the witness Kahrimann will not appear for cross-examination and that therefore you withdraw the material submitted under 92 bis?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's, then, on the record. Then is it correct, Mr. Gaynor, that Prosecution Exhibit 740, which was introduced through the witness Selak, that you seek the admission of the pages 1 to 6 of the transcript of the video?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's correct. And pages 1 to 7 of the B/C/S translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And 1 to 7 of the B/C/S translation. So 1 to 6 for the English; 1 to 7 for the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I have copies here for Your Honour and for the Registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If you'd please be so kind to provide them to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: This is P740.A and P740.A.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then the -- it was indicated in court on the 14th of July that you'd like to have the transcript in the Blaskic case of the evidence of Mr. Kaiser to be admitted. I do understand it was Ms. Richterova who told us that. I -- we have been informed by now that the application to have the Blaskic transcript in evidence is withdrawn. Is that a correct understanding?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, our application in respect of that transcript is withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then that is clear. Then for the information of the parties, the Kotor Varos dossier - I think it was tab 4 in the Kotor Varos dossier - on the index it indicated that I think the 57th or 58th and 59th Session were in under tab 4, where only the 58th was. The Chamber has ex officio corrected the index attached to the Kotor Varos dossier to the extent that only the 58th Session is found under tab 4. I also do understand that now for the Bratunac dossier the registrar, on the basis of what the Prosecution has said on the 15th of June, under tab 1 of the Bratunac dossier all minutes of meetings other than the three the OTP wished to be admitted into evidence are by Madam Registrar now removed from the original of the Kotor Varos dossier and the parties are invited to do the same. And which three are remaining can be found in the transcript of the hearing of the 15th of June. As far as the Foca dossier is concerned, the B/C/S translation of tab 6 was missing from the dossier. On the 6th of July, the Office of the Prosecution has tendered the missing translation to all parties, and Madam Registrar has now placed that translation in the original of the Foca -- of the Foca binder, the Foca dossier. Then there were some documents Mr. Krajisnik has handed up in relation to the witnesses Bjelobrk, Prstojevic and Topajic and Witness 680. These have been sent for translation and we hope to receive the translation very soon. These were the technical and perhaps not that much exciting procedural matters I would like -- I wished to bring to your attention. Let me just ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We still have to deal with today's exhibits, but we are not going to ask more from the patience of the interpreters and the technicians and we'll have to find a moment to -- to deal with them. We adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, Courtroom I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 21st day of July, 2005, at 9.00 a.m. 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
